title: 2004 HMMT February General Round 2 Problem 2
statement: Andrea flips a fair coin repeatedly, continuing until she either flips two heads in a row (the sequence \(H H\) ) or flips tails followed by heads (the sequence \(T H\) ). What is the probability that she will stop after flipping \(H H\) ?

solutions.text:
\(\square\)
The only way that Andrea can ever flip \(H H\) is if she never flips \(T\), in which case she must flip two heads immediately at the beginning. This happens with probability \(\frac{1}{4}\).
